records.name: St. Timothy Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation on Fillmore Street in Fox Chase with a Sunday 9:15 am service that includes Holy Communion. Its site has a section for newcomers.
records.what_you_do: Attend the Sunday 9:15 am service and stay for coffee hour, read the newcomer page, or stop by the office on a Tuesday or Thursday morning. Members also serve through ministries such as a monthly free community lunch (Hope's Table) and a group that cooks meals for homebound neighbors.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 9:15 am to 10:15 am, with Holy Communion and a coffee hour afterward. The office is open Tuesday and Thursday, 9 am to noon.

cost.text: The site does not mention dues or fees for worship or the ministries.

first_step.how: Come to the 9:15 am Sunday service, stay for coffee hour, and ask to meet the pastor or a member. You can also call the office on a Tuesday or Thursday morning.
first_step.basis: The site has an I'm New page that invites newcomers to come to a service, talk with members at coffee hour, or call the office. It does not describe a welcome class.
first_step.what_to_expect: The service runs one hour, from 9:15 am to 10:15 am, and includes Holy Communion, music, and a short message for children told as a story by the pastor. Afterward, a coffee hour with bakery treats gives you a chance to talk with members. The site does not mention dues or fees.
first_visit_tips: Park in the large lot across from the Fillmore Street entrance.
Dress however you feel comfortable; the site says plenty of people wear business casual, jeans or team hoodies, and that showing up matters most.
Stay for coffee hour to meet people.
Call the office on a Tuesday or Thursday between 9 am and noon if you have questions first.

records.notes: The site is current: its events page lists October 2026 items, including the weekly Sunday worship with Communion on Oct 11, 2026 and a free community lunch (Hope's Table) on Oct 10, 2026. Most events on that page are St. Timothy Preschool items, which are not part of this record. The news page has no written dates. No page read says anything about wheelchair access, so that stays unknown. Parking is in the tips because it is a practical visit detail, not an access statement. The site does not describe adult classes, the length of coffee hour, or what children do during the service beyond the pastor's message. Hope's Table has no day, time or place on the ministries page, so it is not in the schedule. Tier 1 had this group as probably_active; October 2026 events make it active.

records.name: St. Timothy Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Levick and Battersby Streets in the Northeast with a 6:30 am and a 9:15 am Sunday Mass, and weekday Mass in the lower church.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass. The archdiocese listing names a religious education coordinator and an outreach sister, with no program details.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 6:30 am in the lower church and 9:15 am in the upper church. Saturday vigil Mass at 4 pm in the upper church. Weekday Mass Tuesday to Saturday at 8:30 am in the lower church. Saturday confession 3 to 3:45 pm.

first_step.how: Come to the 9:15 am Sunday Mass in the upper church, or the 6:30 am Mass in the lower church. Call the rectory at 215-624-6188 with questions.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and a rectory phone is published, but the pages we could read describe no newcomer group or orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. The 9:15 am Sunday Mass is in the upper church, while the 6:30 am Sunday Mass and the weekday Masses are in the lower church. The archdiocese listing does not say how long Mass runs or what happens afterward.
first_visit_tips: Check which level of the church your Mass is held in before you go.
Saturday confession runs 3 to 3:45 pm if you want to speak with a priest.
Call the rectory if you need help with access, since the listing does not confirm access for this building.

records.notes: The parish's own site (st-tims.org) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on its homepage, so it was not read and was not retried. Mass times, address, phone and staff names come from the archdiocese parish listing, which also lists a Saturday vigil at 4 pm that tier 1 did not have. The site's email sits behind a protected link, so no email is recorded. Newcomer friendliness stays at 3 because no newcomer or outreach program is described on the pages read. The archdiocese listing says the page was updated one year ago with no year written, so it is not used as dated evidence. Recheck st-tims.org when it is reachable.

records.name: St. Vincent de Paul Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Price and Lena Streets in Germantown with Sunday Masses at 9 and 10:30 am and weekday Masses at 7 am. It lists nearly 75 ministries.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, then look at the ministries list. Several groups meet on set days, such as a weekly food pantry on Tuesday mornings, a Wednesday evening Bible study, a Thursday evening choir, and a monthly Centering Prayer group, and most list a contact.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 9 am and 10:30 am; the 10:30 am Mass is livestreamed. Weekday Mass Monday to Saturday at 7 am. Saturday vigil Mass at 4 pm. Adoration follows the first Saturday 7 am Mass until 9 am in the rectory chapel. Confession by appointment.

first_step.how: Come to the 9 am or 10:30 am Sunday Mass, then call the parish office at 215-438-2925 to ask about the New Parishioner Orientation, which the site says is just getting started.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the office phone is listed. The site mentions a new parishioner orientation that is just starting, but gives no date or sign-up steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday Mass is at 9 am or 10:30 am, and the 10:30 am Mass is livestreamed. Children have their own Liturgy of the Word at both Sunday Masses, so families can bring kids. Mass is free, and the site does not say how long a Mass runs or what happens afterward.
first_visit_tips: Families can ask about the children's Liturgy of the Word at the 9 am and 10:30 am Masses.
Watch the 10:30 am Mass livestream on the parish website or YouTube first if you want a preview.
Look at the ministries list to find a group that meets on a day that works for you.
Ask the office about the New Parishioner Orientation before you start.

records.notes: The parish's own site has dated 2026 items: a 175th anniversary Mass on Sept 27, 2026, an information session on welcoming newcomers from the New Sanctuary Movement committee on Oct 10, 2026, and a celebration video added on 10/6/2026, which sets the last sign of life. Tier 1 said the 9 am Sunday Mass was livestreamed; the site says the 10:30 am Mass is, so that is corrected. The Saturday vigil at 4 pm is added. The ministries page lists nearly 75 groups; only those with set times are named here. The youth and young adult center address from tier 1 does not appear on any page read, so it is dropped. A guessed new-parishioners page returned 404, so orientation details are not available. Partner groups named on the ministries page are in leads_only, with no own website identified.

records.name: St. William Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Rising Sun Avenue in the Northeast with Masses in Spanish, Pakistani-Urdu and Creole, and weekday Masses at 6:30 am and noon.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in the language you prefer. The archdiocese listing names a religious education coordinator, a Hispanic ministry priest and a Haitian apostolate chaplain, but gives no group meeting times.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 7:30 am, 9 am and 10:30 am in Spanish, at 12:30 pm (October to May), at 2 pm in Pakistani-Urdu, at 5 pm in Haitian Creole, and at 8 pm (October to May). Weekday Mass at 6:30 am and noon. Saturday Mass at 8 am and vigil at 5 pm. Confession Saturdays at 4 pm and on Thursdays before First Fridays from 12:30 to 1 pm.

locations.label: Church (Rising Sun Ave. and Devereaux St.)
locations.address: Rising Sun Ave. and Devereaux St.

access.notes: The archdiocese listing describes ramps, curb cuts and wide doors at the church entrances in general terms, and a meeting room restroom adapted for wheelchair users. It says to confirm these for this building. Elevator and hearing assistance are not mentioned.

first_step.how: Choose the Mass in the language you prefer, such as the 9 am Spanish Mass, the 2 pm Pakistani-Urdu Mass or the 5 pm Haitian Creole Mass, or call the rectory at 215-745-1389 to ask which one fits.
first_step.basis: Every Mass is open to the public and the rectory phone is published. No group is described as open to newcomers, and the ministries list no meeting times.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and the times are grouped by language, so check the list for the one you want. Most Masses are in the lower church, while the 12:30 pm and 8 pm Masses (October to May) and the 5 pm Creole Mass are in the upper church. The listing does not say how long Mass lasts or what happens afterward.
first_visit_tips: A few Mass times do not name a language, so call the rectory if you are unsure which one to attend.
Confession is on Saturdays at 4 pm if you want to speak with a priest before Mass.
Check which level of the church your Mass is in, since most are in the lower church.

records.notes: The parish's own site (churchofstwilliam.com) returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on its homepage, so it was not read and was not retried. Every fact here comes from the archdiocese parish listing, which names the language for most Masses. Parking and transit are not stated anywhere read. The listing says the page was updated three months ago with no year written, so it is not used as dated evidence. Wheelchair access stays unknown until the building is confirmed.

records.name: Starfinder Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia soccer nonprofit with Short Shots for children ages 2 to 6, the Playmakers leadership program for students in grades 9 to 12, school and camp programs, leagues and tournaments.
records.what_you_do: Families sign children up for Short Shots through the registration link on the site. Students in grades 9 to 12 apply to Playmakers at application days or open houses. The foundation also hires coaches for after-school and evening programs.

schedule.text: Short Shots runs in six-week sessions, once a week for an hour, on Saturdays from 11 am to noon, all year. Playmakers is a six-month program for students in grades 9 to 12 and takes applications at application days and open houses.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the site. The Short Shots page says financial help is available for families who need it.

first_step.how: For Short Shots (ages 2 to 6), register through the registration link on the Short Shots page. For Playmakers, RSVP for an application day or open house through the link on the site.
first_step.basis: The Playmakers page says all skill levels are welcome, and each program has a sign-up link on the site.
first_step.what_to_expect: Short Shots is a 60-minute class once a week for six weeks, held on Saturdays from 11 am to noon. Each class is an hour of active play, skill building and games for children ages 2 to 6. The site does not name the class location or say whether parents may stay, so ask when you register.
first_visit_tips: Register through the Short Shots link before you come, since sign-up is needed.
Ask where the class meets when you register, because the site does not name the field.
Ask about financial help when you register if cost is a concern.
For Playmakers, the fall application days and open houses are listed without a year, so confirm the current dates when you RSVP.

records.notes: The homepage lists a Cocktails with a Kick! 2026 event with no month, and Playmakers application days and open houses without a year. Neither is used to set the date, so status stays probably_active on the January 2, 2025 news item, the newest item with a full date. The Playmakers page at two guessed URLs returned 404, so Playmakers details come from the homepage only. Facebook post text was not used for any date. The Short Shots page lists a separate question line, 267-670-2705; the record keeps the main office phone. The contact name Heidi Warren from the IRS record was removed: the foundation's own news shows a leadership change in 2020, and no current contact person is named on the pages read. Class location is not named on any page read; the Main Street address is the foundation office.

records.name: The Steelers Youth Athletic Club
records.summary: A youth athletic club with football, basketball and baseball, cheerleading and dance, and a financial literacy program. It is looking for coaches and mentors.
records.what_you_do: Kids register through the REGISTER form on the site. Adults can sign up as coaches through the Join the Program form, and mentors and mentees each have their own sign-up form.

locations.label: Mc Ilvain Park, Philadelphia (listed in the site footer)

cost.text: The site does not list a registration fee. It asks for donations, with no set amount.

first_step.how: Use the REGISTER form on the site to sign a child up, or the Join the Program form to sign up as a coach. Mentors and mentees each have a separate form.
first_step.basis: The sign-up forms are public and the club says it is looking for coaches and mentors. The site gives no season, practice days, times or place, so a first visit is hard to picture.
first_visit_tips: Email the club to ask about the season, practice days, times and place before you register.
Ask about the fee when you register, since the site does not list one.

records.notes: The club's site lists its programs and sign-up forms, but gives no season, practice days or times, age ranges, fees, or practice place. The guessed About and Join the Program pages returned 404, so the form is described from the homepage only. The footer copyright reads 2021; copyright footers are not evidence, so status stays probably_active on the basis of a working site with no dates. One web search found no independent public source for this club. Its results were about the Pittsburgh Steelers team and unrelated clubs, and none ties this club to that team. Cheerleading and dance has no matching interest tag, so it appears in the summary only. The footer names Mc Ilvain Park, but the site does not say practices happen there. Schedule text from tier 1 is left in place because nothing new could be established.

records.name: Stella Maris Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at 10th and Bigler Streets in South Philadelphia with Sunday Masses at 8 and 10:30 am and a Saturday vigil at 5 pm.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass. The archdiocese listing names parish staff but no community programs.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am and 10:30 am. Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm. Weekday Mass Tuesday to Saturday at 8 am. Saturday confession 4 to 4:45 pm.

locations.label: Church (SE corner of 10th and Bigler Sts.)

access.notes: The archdiocese listing says the church and a meeting room are accessible, and that the church restroom has wheelchair features. It does not mention an elevator.

first_step.how: Come to the 8 am or 10:30 am Sunday Mass, or call the rectory at 215-465-2336 with questions.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and the rectory phone is published. No newcomer program is described on the archdiocese listing, and the parish's own site could not be opened.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone. Sunday Masses are at 8 am and 10:30 am, with a Saturday vigil at 5 pm and weekday Masses at 8 am from Tuesday to Saturday. The listing names parish staff but no groups, so calling the rectory is the best way to ask about getting involved.
first_visit_tips: The church is on the southeast corner of 10th and Bigler Streets.
Confession is on Saturdays from 4 to 4:45 pm if you want to speak with a priest.
Call the rectory with access questions, since the listing does not cover parking.

records.notes: The parish's own site could not be read: its TLS certificate has expired, both with and without www, so the homepage was not read. Everything here comes from the archdiocese listing, including the accessibility statement. Parking, transit and any newcomer group are not stated on that listing. The listing says the page was updated two years ago with no year written, so it is not used as dated evidence. Recheck the parish site when it is reachable, since it may carry more detail.
